question.text: This modern-day Balkan country staged a decades-long revolt against Ottoman rule in the 15th century led by Skanderbeg. In the 20th century, it was ruled by the dictator Enver Hoxha (HOE-juh).
question.clue: Italy invaded this country during World War II when it was ruled by a man who claimed descent from Skanderbeg.

swap.leadin: Its source is in the Black Forest region of Germany.
swap.text: Name this river that flows through Vienna long before it reaches the Black Sea.
swap.clue: Despite not being native to it, the Phanariotes served as administrators of a region on this river.

question.text: This former Yugoslav President was tried for war crimes at The Hague, but died in prison in of a heart attack in 2006 while still awaiting a verdict.
question.clue: He was overthrown in the 2000 Bulldozer Revolution.

swap.leadin: This country was once ruled by Nicolae Ceausescu.
swap.text: Name this country, whose capital Bucharest lies on the banks of the Dambovita River.
swap.clue: After Decree 770 all but banned contraception and abortion here, abusive orphanages such as Cighid filled with babies.

question.text: This eventual assassin of Franz Ferdinand was unable to act after the initial failure by Cabrinovic. He was imprisoned and eventually died of tuberculosis in his cell.
question.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

swap.text: This general was the leader of Army of the Republika Srpska (serp-ska) and oversaw the massacre of Bosniaks at Srebrenica and the Siege of Sarajevo. This earned him the nickname the "Butcher of Bosnia."
swap.clue: Of course, the Serbs were trying to do their own version of ethnic cleansing - this Serb was arrested on May 26, 2011 for war crimes including orchestrating the Siege of Sarajevo and the 1995 Srebrenica massacre.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the career of Brazilian diplomat Sergio Vieira de Mello.
question.text: He served as the first Special Representative of the Secretary General to this country, which at the time had declared independence from Serbia. NATO conducted bombing campaigns in this country as part of Operation Noble Anvil.
question.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

swap.leadin: The Byzantine Empire had many foreign allies.
swap.text: The Byzantines received the support of these people during the 717-718 Siege of Constantinople under the leadership of their khan Tervel. The future Byzantine emperor Basil II earned the epithet of these peoples' "slayer."
swap.clue: The emperor Nikephoros I had his skull turned into a silver cup after he was killed by some of these people at the battle of Pliska, at which their leader was Krum.

question.leadin: Cardinal Aloysius Stepinac was imprisoned for allegedly supporting this organization.
question.text: Name this Nazi-aligned fascist organization led by Ante Pavelic that ruled Croatia during World War 2.
question.clue: Along with the Nazi party, the Bigelow Report outed the Roman Catholic church for hiding this organization's gold.

swap.leadin: This man was rumored to have banned the word "Dracula" in his country after he was taunted with that name on a 1978 visit to the United States.
swap.text: Name this leader who promoted protochronism, which absurdly claimed that his country originated various cultural accomplishments attributed to others. This author of the July Theses was kept in power through a secret police known as the Securitate (seh-koo-rih-TAH-tay).
swap.clue: Thousands of orphans were crammed into orphanages such as Cighid during this man's reign.

question.leadin: For speaking out against the regime of this country, dissident Georgi Markov was assassinated in London with a ricin pellet shot out of an umbrella gun.
question.text: Name this country whose first communist leader was Georgi Dimitrov. It was ruled for most of the Cold War by Todor Zhivkov.
question.clue: This country was defeated in the Second Balkan War and led by Tsar Boris III during World War II.

swap.leadin: Though famous for other reasons, this man was known as a playwright and novelist throughout his life, authoring such works as The Truth that Killed.
swap.text: Name this dissident who was assassinated in London in 1978. The murder has been traced to a secret service agent codenamed "Piccadilly", whose real identity is often suspected to be the Danish citizen Francesco Gullino.
swap.clue: This Bulgarian dissident who was infamously assassinated in 1978 when a pellet containing ricin was fired from an umbrella into his leg.

question.leadin: This city began enforcing the first state-mandated traveler quarantine in the 14th century.
question.text: Name this city that, per the Treaty of Zadar, was placed under Hungarian control after its transfer from Venice.
question.clue: The nobles of this city elected its leaders to a position known as either Rector or knez ("k'nez").

swap.text: This Croatian nobleman helped quash the Magyar rebellion in order to gain favor for his people with Austria. He issued a proclamation that abolished serfdom in Croatia.

question.text: This man joined with the Iron Guard to establish the National Legionary State in 1940, but was overthrown by the return of King Michael for his Nazi collaboration.
question.clue: This leader's army launched Operation Munchen to reclaim Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina, and massacred Jews in Odessa and Iasi.

swap.text: The legend that Elizabeth Bathory bathed in the blood of her virgin victims has led some to assign her vampiric qualities, calling her "Countess Dracula" in reference to this Wallachian prince who impaled many of his prisoners.
swap.answerHtml: Vlad III Dracula [or Vlad the Impaler; or Vlad Tepes]
swap.clue: This voivode of Wallachia who led the Night Attack against Mehmed II in 1462. He was captured by Matthias Corvinus of Hungary later that year.

question.leadin: Answer the following about ugly politics behind the Iron Curtain.
question.text: Together with Petru Groza, this Romanian leader reportedly held King Michael at gunpoint to convince him to abdicate. After becoming prime minister in 1952, he forged alliances with China and other non-communist states, before being succeeded as party leader by Nicolae Ceausescu ("chow-SHES-koo").
question.clue: This patron of Nicolae Ceausescu was the Communist leader of Romania from 1948 to 1965. Domestically, he emphasized the manufacturing of consumer goods, while he sought to improve foreign relations with both the West and China.

swap.leadin: Name some fields in European history which have really cool names.
swap.text: The Serbian prince Lazar was crushed at this field during the Battle of Kosovo in 1389, while Milos Obilic got some revenge by stabbing Murad I.

question.leadin: He was a Pannonian chieftain who took advantage of Charlemagne's conquest of the Avars to establish his own throne. FTPE.
question.text: Name this khan, whose son and successor Omurtag persecuted Christians.

swap.leadin: An "old" faction led by Janez Bleiweis within this ethnic group clashed with a "young" faction in the second half of the 19th century over how radically to oppose Austrian rule.
swap.text: Name this ethnic group, the primary inhabitants of the Duchy of Carniola. Following WWI, they formed a namesake kingdom with Serbs and Croats.
swap.clue: In 1918, Peter I's kingdom expanded to form Yugoslavia, composed of Serbs, Croats, and this ethnic group. This ethnic group's namesake republic, which includes Melania Trump's birthplace in Novo Mesto, was the first country to break from Yugoslavia in 1990.
